finding.title: Add ref.mounted guards and Timer disposal to SignInController's autoDispose async flows

evidence.quote:
final watchdog = Timer(const Duration(seconds: 15), () {
      if (state is SignInSubmitting) {

finding.why: This 1016-line Notifier<SignInState> is registered autoDispose and performs 84 awaited operations per file (multi-second retries, 8s Firestore timeouts, 350ms polling loops) yet contains zero occurrences of 'mounted' anywhere in the file — every method touches `state`/`_ref` after an await with no disposal guard. If the user backs out of the sign-in screen mid-request (a completely ordinary action while a 'signing in...' spinner shows), autoDispose tears the notifier down; when the pending await resolves and the code does `state = SignInError(...)` or `_ref.read(...)`, Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException. The watchdog Timer compounds this: it is only cancelled in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle's own `finally` block, never via ref.onDispose, so if the notifier is disposed mid-flight the Timer keeps running and fires `state = ...` against an already-disposed notifier up to 45s later. The codebase already has an established ref.mounted convention elsewhere (dashboard_providers.dart, notification_providers.dart, sacred_location_provider.dart all use it), so this file's total omission is an inconsistency, not a repo-wide non-issue.
finding.recommendation: After every await that precedes a `state =` or `_ref.read(...)` write, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;`. Register `ref.onDispose(watchdog.cancel)` immediately after each Timer is created (both the 15s and 45s watchdogs).
acceptance_criteria: A notifier test that disposes the ProviderContainer (or pops the route) while signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle is mid-await asserts no exception escapes and no post-dispose state write occurs
Watchdog Timers are cancelled by ref.onDispose in addition to the existing finally-block cancel
